compsNote: No suitable competitor within 1 km, so the nearest within 2 to 3 km are used. Near-twins come first: up to two condos within 1.5 km with a similar number of homes (half to double) completed in 2016 or later. Then every suitable condo within 1 km (same tenure, completed 2011 or later first), widening to 2 km and 3 km only if fewer than 3; executive condos are left out. Resale prices are URA medians for the last 6 months where there were at least 5 resales, otherwise the last 12 months. Condos launched before June 2023 measured their areas under the old rules (including air-con ledges), so their psf is raised 5% to compare like for like.
priceDecide: Like for like by size: for each unit type we take each resale competitor's average psf for units within about 15% of that size (last 6 months, or 12 or 24 if too few). Where a competitor has too few resales of a size, that size is estimated from its own nearest size, so every unit type is judged against the same competitors. Each is raised by a new-launch premium that rises with each competitor's age (21% to 34% here): launches selling now in the OCR charge about 9% over a just-completed resale and about 2.5 points more for each year of its age (29 launches against 102 of their resale competitors, this one and the 6 most extreme pairs left out). Buy at or below = the average of the competitors' new-launch equivalents for that size (a launch nearby from the last 2 years counts for half); walk away above = 5% more. 2-bed: buy at or below $2,430, walk away above $2,550, this project about $2,862 psf; 3-bed: buy at or below $2,610, walk away above $2,740, this project about $2,865 psf; 4-bed: buy at or below $2,480, walk away above $2,600, this project about $2,951 psf. supply.ring: middle ring (6 to 11 km from the CBD)
concerns: Will too many new condos nearby hurt my price?

Besides this project's own 515 homes, about 2,783 new homes within 2 km launch within about 2 years of it (Bayshore Drive (mixed-use GLS), Bagnall Haus, Bedok Rise (GLS), New Upper Changi Road (GLS)); the condo resale market within 2 km handles about 579 resales a year. Our test of 19 condos completed 2016 to 2022 in the middle ring (6 to 11 km from the CBD): those with more than 862 other new homes completing within 2 km and 2 years grew 1.9% a year over the past 4 years, against 3.6% for those with fewer (URA caveats). That points to a real drag on resale prices around completion: plan to hold longer, and pick the unit types and stacks that stand out.
The developer paid more for the land. Am I paying more?

Across 16 launches since 2023, launch prices rose roughly dollar for dollar with break-even (about $103 per $100), so developers kept a similar dollar margin while their percentage margin shrank (22% above break-even on land of $1,200 psf ppr or more, 31% on cheaper land). Part of that is location: dearer land is usually where homes sell for more anyway. So a high bid does show up in prices, but only as far as buyers will pay against nearby homes. The test that protects you is the price against same-size competitors: our buy-at and walk-away prices.
Will the developer cut prices later?

77% sold so far. Developers must sell every unit within 5 years of buying the land or repay most of a 40% stamp duty (IRAS); with many units left, late discounts or deals on slower stacks are possible as the deadline nears, but the best stacks rarely get cheaper.
Should I wait for the next launch nearby?

The next launch nearby, New Upper Changi Road (GLS), is likely at about $3,230 psf, above this project's 3-bed. Waiting for it is unlikely to get you a cheaper new home here, and a dearer neighbour helps support this project's resale price.

Islandwide, about 18,296 private homes complete in 2027 and 2028 and 15,810 homes in the pipeline were still unsold at mid-2026 (URA). That is enough to keep price growth moderate, but local supply and the local buyer pool matter more for your resale.
